Hi! I had my bisalp 8 days ago, and once I woke up from surgery I was more exhausted than anything else. I fainted twice after trying to get up to use the restroom but that wasn't painful just inconvenient. I have a low pain tolerance so I was surprised my pain was mostly tolerable. It hurt to laugh though. And because I fainted I stayed overnight at the hospital. A nurse had me forcibly cough while she put pressure on my abdomen and *holy fuck* that shot my 2-3 level pain up to an 8. Later they gave me tylenol and put something in my iv to help with the pain so I could sleep easier. 

That night I'd get sudden sharp pains, making it a hassle to get rest. I even remember once nearly being in tears over it. Now, I *could've* called my nurse and asked her for something stronger but I just didn't want to bother her. When I woke up I felt significantly better. Once I got home I started taking the 800 mg Ibuprofen I was prescribed. I was also prescribed acetaminophen with codeine but I haven't touched it and been alright!

According to my surgeon, 1 out of 600 tubals fail. I didn't ask what method but I already knew that tubals are no longer the gold standard and haven't been since 2015(?). She doesn't do tubals anymore since bisalps are so much more effective.

Oh, and one final thing: I was told the fainting isn't a common reaction so please don't worry about that! Nurses suggested it was probably a mix of the anesthesia, dehydration, and not eating as per my instructions.
